properties.statement:
A DesignRule IS THE ONLY GOVERNANCE NODE WITH NO TYPED CONSTRUCTOR, AND TWO INDEPENDENT PROJECTS HIT IT WITHOUT KNOWING OF EACH OTHER. dev_storyflow 2026-08-23 ('there is no `add_design_rule`, so a DesignRule can only be written through the generic `create_node`, and its field names are discoverable only by `describe_schema` — which I ran only AFTER guessing wrong') and the qs project 2026-09-04, on its FIRST use ('DesignRule has no constructor... `find_tools("design rule convention")` did not surface anything relevant, which is a discoverability miss on top of the missing constructor').

CONFIRMED 2026-09-04: no `add_design_rule` anywhere in reflow2-mcp. Every other governance-shaped node has one.

⭐ TWO PROJECTS IS THE SIGNAL. One report is a preference; two independent ones on the same missing call, one of them from a first-time user who also failed to FIND it via `find_tools`, is a surface defect. And it sits under ACCEPTED intent — `req:declared-vocabulary-is-reachable-from-the-surface` — so this is an unbuilt half of something already agreed, not a new want.

🛑 AND ONE HALF OF THE qs REPORT IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT — acting on it would have BROKEN A DELIBERATE DESIGN. They wrote: '`enforced` defaults to true, so a rule recorded without thought claims to gate merges.' PROBED DIRECTLY: created a DesignRule through `create_node` with `name`, `statement` and `category` and no `enforced`. The stored node came back carrying `category`, `name`, `statement` AND NO `enforced` FIELD AT ALL. `schema/core.yaml:129` states the design in as many words: 'THREE STATES: true = gate-blocking (and owes a detector); false = advisory; ABSENT = nobody has stated it, reported as unstated and never read as enforced. NEVER DEFAULTED: whether breaking a rule should stop somebody's build is a policy about consequence, and it is the user's to state.'

⚠️ SO THE REPORTED SYMPTOM IS REAL AND ITS DIAGNOSIS IS NOT. Something did make them believe the rule claimed to gate merges — most likely `unstated_rule_enforcement` firing on the absent value, which is the detector CORRECTLY reporting 'nobody has stated it' and reads to a newcomer as an accusation. That is a WORDING defect in the gap, not a defaulting defect in the schema, and the two have opposite fixes: one rewords a question, the other would delete a three-state design that was argued for on purpose.

THE FIX THE TWO REPORTS AGREE ON: a typed `add_design_rule` carrying `name`, `statement`, `category`, optional `enforced` — and, from qs, a `find_tools` entry that answers 'design rule convention'.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether other node types are equally unreachable. Only DesignRule was checked, and only because two reports named it.
